Classification guard: the single authored edge asserts association only (etiologicalConsensus NOT_ESTABLISHED, hypothesizedOnly:true). It records that ichthyosis cohorts show reduced tear-film stability and ocular surface changes in the presence of eyelid malformation, not that ichthyosis caused dry-eye disease in any individual; the located studies are small single-centre cohorts without controls, mean aqueous tear production was within normal limits, and an individual claim therefore requires ocular surface examination with dates, documentation of eyelid position and malformation, symptom history, and exclusion of the competing causes of ocular surface disease listed on the edge.

Duplicate-scope guard: the dry-eye-syndrome identity receives no prior incoming window, so this batch opens the first condition-specific window on that target; no visual-impairment edge is authored from ichthyosis because the located condition-specific series records an excellent visual prognosis with timely surgical repair of the eyelid malformation, no corneal-scarring edge is authored because perforation was documented in only two of eleven patients in a single surgical-access-dependent series, and no cellulitis/impetigo edge is authored because no ichthyosis-specific infection denominators were located (zero-record, magnitude, and entity-specificity guards).
governanceNotes: D1 batch 47 (2026-09-24): one bounded association edge authored - ichthyosis to dry-eye-syndrome (rank 1), ASSOCIATION_ONLY with etiologicalConsensus NOT_ESTABLISHED, vaNexusProbabilityAlignment NOT_ASSERTED, hypothesizedOnly:true, and mechanismCategory MECHANICAL_OR_COMPRESSIVE (eyelid malformation with tear-film instability and altered ocular surface). The proposition rests on the Palamar 2015 cohort of twelve patients with lamellar ichthyosis in which mean tear break-up time was 6.58 seconds in both eyes - below the conventional ten-second threshold for tear-film stability - with ocular surface staining grades of 0.36 and 0.39 and preserved mean Schirmer 1 aqueous production of 18.75 mm, and whose conclusion states that in lamellar ichthyosis eyelid malformations together with decreased tear break-up time might cause sight-threatening complications; and on the Al-Amry 2016 retrospective series of eleven ichthyosis patients in which bilateral ectropion was the most common ocular diagnosis, most patients required skin grafting for eyelid ectropion, and two patients developed corneal perforation with poor prognosis, while visual prognosis remained excellent with timely surgical intervention. The edge is not raised to causation: the cohorts are small, single-centre, and uncontrolled with a mean patient age under twenty in the lamellar cohort, aqueous tear production was preserved, and coexisting blepharitis, meibomian disease, retinoid exposure, and age-related ocular surface disease are not excluded.

Counter-evidence and magnitude screens recorded 2026-09-24: (i) visual prognosis - the ichthyosis series explicitly records an excellent visual prognosis when eyelid malformation is surgically repaired in time, with corneal perforation in two of eleven patients, so a visual-acuity edge would overstate the located evidence and the window is bounded to ocular surface disease (magnitude and target-specificity guard); (ii) aqueous tear production - Schirmer 1 values were within normal limits in the lamellar cohort, so the located abnormality is tear-film stability and lid-related, not a primary aqueous-deficient process, which is why the mechanism is mechanical rather than secretory; (iii) syndromic versus generic identity - sensorineural deafness and keratitis in ichthyosis occur in the distinct keratitis-ichthyosis-deafness syndrome, which is a separate genetic entity from the generic ichthyosis identity, so no hearing-loss edge is authored (entity-mismatch guard); (iv) infection - barrier failure is a plausible mechanism, but the located search returned generic cellulitis reviews and no ichthyosis-specific infection denominator, so no infection edge is authored (zero-record guard).

Negative screens recorded 2026-09-24: (i) no visual-impairment edge - the located series records excellent visual prognosis with timely eyelid surgery and visual loss only through rare corneal perforation (magnitude and target-specificity guards); (ii) no corneal-scarring edge - perforation in two of eleven patients in one surgical-access-dependent series is too thin for a chronic corneal-outcome edge at this time, and it should be reopened if a cohort reports keratopathy prevalence with denominators (zero-record guard); (iii) no hearing-loss edge - the located deafness evidence is syndrome-specific to keratitis-ichthyosis-deafness, an entity distinct from the generic ichthyosis identity (entity-mismatch guard); (iv) no cellulitis, impetigo, or fungal-skin-infection edge - no ichthyosis-specific infection denominators were located (zero-record guard); (v) no depressive-disorder, anxiety-disorder, or insomnia edge - no condition-specific ichthyosis psychosocial cohort was located in this batch and the psychosocial windows belong to their own primaries (zero-record and duplicate-scope guards); (vi) no heat-intolerance, hypohidrosis, or hyperthermia edge - no such catalog identities exist (wrong-target guard); (vii) duplicate-scope note: this batch adds the first ichthyosis-primary window to the registry.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Clinical cohorts document ocular surface changes in ichthyosis: the Palamar 2015 study of twelve patients with lamellar ichthyosis found mean tear break-up time of 6.58 seconds in both eyes - below the conventional ten-second threshold - with ocular surface staining grades of 0.36 and 0.39, and concluded that eyelid malformations together with decreased tear break-up time might cause sight-threatening complications, while the Al-Amry 2016 series of eleven ichthyosis patients found bilateral ectropion to be the most common ocular diagnosis, with most patients requiring skin grafting for the eyelid malformation - a reproducible co-occurrence association rather than an individual causal nexus.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation is established: the located cohorts are small, single-centre, and uncontrolled, mean aqueous tear production was preserved, and coexisting blepharitis, meibomian gland disease, retinoid or topical therapy, cicatricial conjunctival disease, and age-related ocular surface disease are not excluded, so an individual determination requires ocular surface examination with tear break-up time, Schirmer testing and staining on dated examinations, documentation of eyelid position and malformation, symptom history, and exclusion of the competing causes of ocular surface disease listed on this edge.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: A hypothesized mechanical route is described: ichthyosis produces cicatricial eyelid malformation - bilateral ectropion was the most common ocular diagnosis in the Al-Amry 2016 series - so the lids fail to appose and blink completely, the tear film is no longer spread and protected, and evaporation increases while the exposed ocular surface becomes keratinised and inflamed, producing tear-film instability and ocular surface staining such as the 6.58-second mean tear break-up time recorded in the Palamar 2015 lamellar cohort; preserved Schirmer 1 values in the same cohort indicate that the abnormality is lid- and stability-related rather than a primary secretory failure, and the small uncontrolled designs leave individual attribution hypothesized.
causalMechanism.secondaryVector: Ichthyosis-associated scaling and abnormal keratinisation of the lid margin and ocular surface, together with meibomian gland involvement and retinoid or topical therapy used for the skin disease, can independently destabilize the tear film and add to the mechanical exposure.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: The edge asserts an association only: two small uncontrolled ichthyosis cohorts document ectropion, reduced tear break-up time, and ocular surface staining, but aqueous tear production was preserved, the samples are single-centre with twelve and eleven patients respectively, and the competing causes of ocular surface disease - blepharitis, meibomian disease, retinoid exposure, cicatricial conjunctivitis, and ageing - are not excluded, so no at-least-as-likely-as-not probability is asserted and an individual claim requires dated ocular surface examination, eyelid documentation, and competing-cause evaluation.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: Ophthalmic examination with tear break-up time, Schirmer testing, ocular surface staining score, and meibomian gland assessment, with dates; documentation of eyelid position and malformation (ectropion, lagophthalmos) and any surgical repair with dates; ocular symptoms and their relation to the skin disease course; documentation of the ichthyosis subtype and genetic or clinical diagnosis, and of all topical and systemic therapies including retinoids; evaluation for competing causes including blepharitis, meibomian gland dysfunction, cicatricial conjunctivitis or pemphigoid, Sjogren syndrome and other autoimmune disease, medication effects, contact lens use, and age-related ocular surface disease; ophthalmology or dermatology assessment of whether the ichthyosis and its eyelid malformation materially contributed to the ocular surface disease
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Primary aqueous-deficient dry eye including Sjogren syndrome and other autoimmune causes
Medication-related ocular surface disease (retinoids, antihistamines, topical agents)
Cicatricial conjunctival disease such as ocular pemphigoid or Stevens-Johnson sequelae
Age-related or environmental ocular surface disease and contact lens-related disease

suggestions.rationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY: a twelve-patient lamellar ichthyosis cohort found mean tear break-up time of 6.58 seconds with ocular surface staining and concluded that eyelid malformations together with decreased tear break-up time might cause sight-threatening complications, and an eleven-patient ichthyosis series found bilateral ectropion to be the most common ocular diagnosis requiring skin grafting in most patients, establishing a reproducible co-occurrence association between ichthyosis-related eyelid malformation and ocular surface disease; the edge is not raised to causation because the cohorts are small, single-centre, and uncontrolled with preserved aqueous tear production and unexcluded competing causes, so the consensus remains NOT_ESTABLISHED with dated ocular surface examination, eyelid documentation, therapy documentation, and competing-cause requirements and no probability estimate is asserted.
